1→# Build session six — brief: the party-facing surface
   2→
   3→**Status at handoff: 2026-09-23.** Suite 273 tests: **the only failures are in
   4→`tests/test_party_surface.py`** (27 tests, one passes trivially today), which is this session's
   5→acceptance target. Read HEAD yourself with `git log -1`.
   6→
   7→Pre-flight:
   8→
   9→```bash
  10→cd ~/hermes-workspace/projects/ryde-build
  11→git status --short           # expect empty
  12→python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .    # expect 273 tests, failures only in test_party_surface
  13→```
  14→
  15→---
  16→
  17→## Why this session exists
  18→
  19→`ui/` is the operator console. The parties have no surface at all: nobody has ever filed a
  20→dispute through a form, and nobody has ever read an outcome. The locked scope says the parties
  21→are **spectators behind a standardized intake form**, the advocates **ask the filing party
  22→targeted follow-up questions only when the form is insufficient**, and the parties receive
  23→either the ruling or the neutral "still under review" message. This session builds that.
  24→
  25→Read `tests/test_party_surface.py` first. Its docstring carries the operator rulings.
  26→
  27→## The deliverable
  28→
  29→Make `tests/test_party_surface.py` pass **without editing it**, keep every other test green,
  30→and ship a party page a non-technical judge understands without explanation.
  31→
  32→### 1. A fourth outcome: `needs_info` (stop and ask, one round)
  33→
  34→Operator ruling 2026-09-23: when either advocate returns follow-up questions, the run **stops
  35→before the Judge**.
  36→
  37→- `app/schemas.py`: add `OUTCOME_NEEDS_INFO = "needs_info"` and `NEEDS_INFO_MESSAGE`, a
  38→  neutral message asking the party for a little more information. It must not mention AI,
  39→  agents, a judge, confidence, or which way the case leans.
  40→- `Resolution` gains `questions_for_party: List[str]`, always serialised (`[]` when none).
  41→  For `needs_info`: `ruling` and `withheld_candidate` are `None`, `delivered_to_parties` and
  42→  `escalated_for_human_review` are `False`.
  43→- `app/pipeline.py`: after both advocates run, collect their questions, the filing party's own
  44→  advocate first, de-duplicated, **capped at 3**. If any, emit `party.notified` with the
  45→  questions and return the case file without calling the Judge. The evidence pack and both
  46→  advocate cases stay on the file.
  47→- **One round only, enforced in code, not in a prompt.** A dispute carrying follow-up answers
  48→  never stops again: the Judge always runs, `questions_for_party` is `[]`, no
  49→  `advocate.follow_up_requested` event is emitted, and `resolution.notes` records that further
  50→  questions were not sent (the note contains the word `follow-up`).
  51→
  52→### 2. Follow-up answers on the dispute
  53→
  54→- `app/dispute.py`: `Dispute.follow_up_answers: List[Dict[str, str]]`, read from
  55→  `ryde_extensions.follow_up_answers` (organiser shape) or top-level `follow_up_answers` (our
  56→  shape). Absent means `[]`. Anything else must be a list of objects each with string
  57→  `question` and string `answer`, or `DisputeError`.
  58→- The case file's `intake` section gains `follow_up_answers` (always present).
  59→- `dispute_block` in `app/agents/base.py` shows the answers to the advocates and the Judge.
  60→
  61→### 3. The mock asks when a form answer is blank
  62→
  63→So the path is demoable before a real model exists. Add to the advocate request metadata:
  64→`filed_by`, `blank_intake_questions` (intake keys whose answer is empty after trimming), and
  65→`has_follow_up_answers`. In `app/llm/mock.py`, only the **filing party's** advocate asks, one
  66→question per blank key, at most 3, and never when `has_follow_up_answers` is true. Keep the
  67→`MOCK` prefix on every string. No shipped record has a blank answer, so none of the 35
  68→existing case runs may change outcome.
  69→
  70→### 4. `app/server.py`: a local server, standard library only
  71→
  72→- `make_server(port, pack_dir=None, out_dir=None, llm=None)` returns an `http.server`
  73→  `ThreadingHTTPServer` bound to **127.0.0.1 only**. `None` means the config default.
  74→  `python3 -m app.server` runs it on port 8000 with the configured LLM provider.
  75→- `party_view(case_file_dict)` returns **exactly** `run_id`, `dispute_id`, `status`,
  76→  `message`, `questions`. Mapping: `ruled` to `decided`, `withheld` to `under_review`,
  77→  `human_review` to `passed_to_support`, `needs_info` to `needs_info`. **Build it from an
  78→  allowlist and fail closed:** any malformed input (not a non-array object, missing or empty
  79→  `party_message`, unknown outcome, `questions_for_party` not a list of strings) returns
  80→  `under_review` with `UNDER_REVIEW_MESSAGE` and no questions. The page is only ever handed
  81→  this view, never the case file.
  82→- `GET /api/trips?category=<c>`: the trips the party can pick from, built from the pack's
  83→  records, in file-name order. Route deviation lists route cases, no-show lists no-show
  84→  cases, any other category lists every trip. Each trip exposes only `trip_id`, `label`,
  85→  `kind`, `pickup`, `dropoff`, `date`, `fare_sgd`. **No names, profiles, ratings, fraud
  86→  flags, GPS or chat.**
  87→- `POST /api/disputes` with `category`, `filed_by`, `trip_id`, `description`,
  88→  `claim_amount_sgd`, `answers`. Build a new record from the pack record for that trip: keep
  89→  the **platform evidence** (trip data, GPS, chat, app events, profiles, cancellation policy)
  90→  and replace **everything the party states** with the form's values. Party-stated fields the
  91→  form does not collect (such as `rider_claims_driver_absent`) are removed, never carried
  92→  over. New `dispute_id` per filing. Run the pipeline, write `dispute.json` beside
  93→  `case_file.json` in the run directory, return `party_view`.
  94→- `POST /api/disputes/<run_id>/answers` with `answers: [{question, answer}]`: 404 for an
  95→  unknown or malformed run id, **409** if that run's outcome is not `needs_info` or it was
  96→  already answered, **400** unless every question the run asked is answered exactly once with
  97→  a non-blank string and nothing else is. Re-run with the answers attached, same
  98→  `dispute_id`, new `run_id`, return `party_view`.
  99→- Validation, all 400: category outside `route_deviation`, `no_show_charge`,
 100→  `property_damage_mess`, `safety_incident`, `other`; `filed_by` not rider or driver; blank or
 101→  over-2000-character description; `claim_amount_sgd` not null and not a number from 0 to 500
 102→  (booleans and strings rejected); an answer key not in that category's questionnaire or a
 103→  non-string answer. Unknown trip is 404. Invalid JSON is 400. A body over 64 KiB is 413.
 104→- Static files: serve `ui/` only (`/` the console, `/party/` the party page). Any path that
 105→  resolves outside `ui/` is 404. The run id and every path are checked **after** decoding.
 106→
 107→### 5. `ui/party/`: the party page (plain HTML, CSS, JS, no framework, no npm)
 108→
 109→A rider files a dispute in three steps: what went wrong (category), which trip, then the
 110→questionnaire, a free-text description and an optional amount. The outcome screen has four
 111→distinct states: **decided** (the message), **under review**, **passed to support**, and
 112→**needs more information** (the questions, each with an answer box, then submit, then the
 113→next outcome). Show the reference number.
 114→
 115→- **Plain language only.** The party never reads the words AI, agent, advocate, judge,
 116→  confidence, withheld, escalate or model anywhere on the page. The test checks this.
 117→- `textContent` only. No `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `document.write`
 118→  or `eval`.
 119→- Label the page as a demo whose trips come from the sample dataset.
 120→- The page is rider-facing in this session. The API accepts `driver`; a driver-side form is
 121→  out of scope.
 122→
 123→### 6. The console renders the fourth outcome
 124→
 125→`ui/app.js`: a `needs_info` case file gets its own state (waiting on the party, the
 126→questions asked, the Judge did not run). A round-two case file shows its follow-up answers.
 127→Older case files without `questions_for_party` or `follow_up_answers` must still render.
 128→
 129→## Rules for this session
 130→
 131→- **Gates live in code, not in prompts.** The one-round limit and the party allowlist are
 132→  Python, not prompt text.
 133→- **Do not edit anything under `tests/`, `tools/` or `data/`.** If a test looks wrong, stop and
 134→  say so.
 135→- Do not change the confidence threshold, the SGD 50 cap, ESC-2, or any policy rule.
 136→- Keep the `MOCK` markers visible.
 137→- **Cut order if the session runs short:** visual polish first. The `needs_info` stop, the
 138→  one-round gate and the fail-closed party view are never cut.
 139→- **A fix is not done until a test fails when it is reverted.** When green, revert the
 140→  one-round gate and the `party_view` fail-closed branch in turn, name the tests that go red,
 141→  restore both.
 142→- Commit in small steps, each with the suite result in the message.
 143→- On a conflict with `docs/statement-extract.md` or `CODEBUDDY.md`, stop and ask.
 144→
 145→## Done means
 146→
 147→```bash
 148→python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .      # 273 tests, OK
 149→python3 -m app.server                           # then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/party/
 150→```

   6→

   9→    filing party, the run stops BEFORE the Judge with a fourth outcome, `needs_info`.

  11→    in code: a dispute that already carries follow-up answers never stops again.
  12→  * The party only ever receives an allowlisted view: status, neutral message, questions.
  13→    A withheld ruling's amount and the Judge's confidence must be structurally absent.

 115→class NeedsInfoOutcome(unittest.TestCase):
 116→    """A blank intake answer stops the run before the Judge, in both record shapes."""
 117→
 118→    def _assert_needs_info(self, case: dict):
 119→        from app.schemas import NEEDS_INFO_MESSAGE, OUTCOME_NEEDS_INFO

 121→        resolution = case["resolution"]

 123→        self.assertEqual("needs_info", OUTCOME_NEEDS_INFO)
 124→        self.assertEqual(NEEDS_INFO_MESSAGE, resolution["party_message"])

 126→        self.assertIsNone(resolution["withheld_candidate"])
 127→        self.assertFalse(resolution["delivered_to_parties"])

   3→These are the shapes the agents must produce and the shapes the rest of the system

   7→Judge output contract (fixed):

  17→A ruling whose confidence is below the configured threshold is not delivered to the

  50→class RulingAction(str, Enum):
  51→    """The ruling enum from the challenge statement. Values are the wire values."""
  52→
  53→    REFUND = "refund"
  54→    COMPENSATION = "compensation"
  55→    NO_ACTION = "no action"

  57→    @classmethod
  58→    def parse(cls, value: Any, *, field_name: str = "action") -> "RulingAction":
  59→        """Parse a model's value into the enum, tolerating underscore/hyphen/case drift."""
  60→        if isinstance(value, RulingAction):
  61→            return value
  62→        if not isinstance(value, str):
  63→            raise ContractError(
  64→                "%s must be one of %s, got %r" % (field_name, _enum_values(), value)
  65→            )
  66→        normalised = re.sub(r"[\s_-]+", " ", value.strip().lower())
  67→        for member in cls:

 268→    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 269→        return {
 270→            "party": self.party,
 271→            "agent": self.agent,
 272→            "claim_summary": self.claim_summary,
 273→            "argument": self.argument,
 274→            "requested_outcome": self.requested_outcome,
 275→            "requested_amount_sgd": self.requested_amount_sgd,
 276→            "evidence_cited": list(self.evidence_cited),
 277→            "policy_rule_ids": list(self.policy_rule_ids),
 278→            "follow_up_questions": list(self.follow_up_questions),
 279→            "validation": self.validation,
 280→            "llm": self.llm,
 281→        }

 283→
 284→@dataclass(frozen=True)
 285→class Resolution:
 286→    """What the system decided, and what the parties are told.
 287→
 288→    `ruling` is set only when a ruling was actually issued to the parties. When the
 289→    confidence gate trips, the Judge's candidate is kept in `withheld_candidate` for the
 290→    human reviewer and `ruling` stays None, so nothing that renders this object
 291→    naively can leak a withheld decision to a party.
 292→    """
 293→
 294→    dispute_id: str
 295→    outcome: str
 296→    party_message: str
 297→    confidence_threshold: float
 298→    ruling: Optional[JudgeRuling] = None
 299→    withheld_candidate: Optional[JudgeRuling] = None
 300→    escalated_for_human_review: bool = False
 301→    notes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
 302→
 303→    @property
 304→    def delivered_to_parties(self) -> bool:
 305→        """True when the parties receive a real decision rather than a holding message."""
 306→        return self.outcome == OUTCOME_RULED
 307→
 308→    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 309→        return {
 310→            "dispute_id": self.dispute_id,
 311→            "outcome": self.outcome,
 312→            "party_message": self.party_message,
 313→            "confidence_threshold": self.confidence_threshold,
 314→            "delivered_to_parties": self.delivered_to_parties,
 315→            "escalated_for_human_review": self.escalated_for_human_review,
 316→            "ruling": self.ruling.to_dict() if self.ruling else None,
 317→            "withheld_candidate": self.withheld_candidate.to_dict() if self.withheld_candidate else None,
 318→            "notes": list(self.notes),
 319→        }
 320→
 321→
 322→def party_message_for_ruling(ruling: JudgeRuling) -> str:
 323→    """The message both parties receive when a ruling is issued."""
 324→    if ruling.action == RulingAction.NO_ACTION.value:
 325→        return "Decision: no action. %s" % ruling.explanation
 326→    return "Decision: %s of SGD %.2f. %s" % (
 327→        ruling.action,
 328→        ruling.recommended_amount_sgd,
 329→        ruling.explanation,
 330→    )

1→"""End-to-end orchestration for one dispute.
   2→
   3→The flow, and the traffic it leaves in the event log:
   4→
   5→    parties  -> system           dispute filed (the intake-form submission)
   6→    system   -> human_review     only for a category outside the two locked ones
   7→    system   -> agents           Evidence Pack built (deterministic, before any LLM call)
   8→    system   -> each advocate    case assigned
   9→    advocate -> judge            case submitted
  10→    advocate -> party            follow-up questions, only when the form is insufficient
  11→    system   -> judge            deliberation started, with both cases
  12→    judge    -> parties          ruling issued, or ruling withheld behind the gate
  13→    system   -> parties          the message the parties actually receive
  14→    system   -> system           run completed
  15→
  16→Nothing here decides anything: the evidence layer computes, the agents argue and rule,
  17→and this module only moves the case between them and records what happened.
  18→"""
  19→
  20→from __future__ import annotations
  21→
  22→import json
  23→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  24→from datetime import datetime, timezone
  25→from pathlib import Path
  26→from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
  27→
  28→from .agents import DriverAdvocate, Judge, RiderAdvocate
  29→from .dispute import Dispute
  30→from .events import Actor, EventLog, EventType
  31→from .evidence import build_evidence_pack
  32→from .llm import LLMClient
  33→from .policy import PolicySet
  34→from .schemas import (
  35→    HUMAN_REVIEW_MESSAGE,
  36→    OUTCOME_HUMAN_REVIEW,
  37→    AdvocateCase,
  38→    Resolution,
  39→)
  40→
  41→CASE_FILE_NAME = "case_file.json"
  42→_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
  43→
  44→
  45→def _policy_source_path(policy: PolicySet) -> str:
  46→    """Serialise the policy path for the case file, anchored to the repo root.
  47→
  48→    Path.resolve() anchors a relative path to the process working directory, so the
  49→    same input produced 'docs/policy.md' from the repo and 'policy.md' from anywhere
  50→    else. Joining to the repo root first makes the output independent of the CWD;
  51→    joining an absolute path is a no-op, so an external policy is unaffected.
  52→    """
  53→    source = Path(policy.source_path)
  54→    resolved = (_REPO_ROOT / source).resolve()
  55→    try:
  56→        return str(resolved.relative_to(_REPO_ROOT))
  57→    except ValueError:
  58→        return source.name
  59→
  60→
  61→@dataclass
  62→class CaseFile:
  63→    """The assembled record of one run: what was claimed, what the evidence showed, what
  64→    was decided, and the event strip. Self-contained so a judge can read one file."""
  65→
  66→    run_id: str
  67→    dispute_id: str
  68→    category: str
  69→    generated_at: str
  70→    confidence_threshold: float
  71→    policy_path: str
  72→    policy_rule_ids: List[str]
  73→    #: What the filing party actually claimed, in their words. The file called itself
  74→    #: self-contained while this lived only in an event payload on disk, so anything
  75→    #: reading case_file.json alone could show the ruling but not the grievance.
  76→    intake: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]
  77→    evidence_pack: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]
  78→    rider_case: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]
  79→    driver_case: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]
  80→    resolution: Dict[str, Any]
  81→    events: List[Dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
  82→
  83→    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
  84→        return {
  85→            "run_id": self.run_id,
  86→            "dispute_id": self.dispute_id,
  87→            "category": self.category,
  88→            "generated_at": self.generated_at,
  89→            "confidence_threshold": self.confidence_threshold,
  90→            "policy": {"source_path": self.policy_path, "rule_ids": self.policy_rule_ids},
  91→            "intake": self.intake,
  92→            "evidence_pack": self.evidence_pack,
  93→            "claims": {"rider": self.rider_case, "driver": self.driver_case},
  94→            "resolution": self.resolution,
  95→            "events": self.events,
  96→        }
  97→
  98→    def write(self, run_dir: Path) -> Path:
  99→        path = Path(run_dir) / CASE_FILE_NAME
 100→        path.write_text(json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=2, default=str) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
 101→        return path
 102→
 103→
 104→def _intake_section(dispute: Dispute) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 105→    """The grievance as filed, for anything reading the case file on its own.
 106→
 107→    The category is carried twice on purpose: `category_as_submitted` is what the party
 108→    picked on the form, `category` is what the router accepted. When they differ, that
 109→    difference is the story of an out-of-scope filing.
 110→    """
 111→    return {
 112→        "filed_by": dispute.filed_by,
 113→        "filed_at": dispute.filed_at,
 114→        "category_as_submitted": dispute.category_as_submitted,
 115→        "claim_text": dispute.claim_text,
 116→        "claim_amount_sgd": dispute.claim_amount_sgd,
 117→        "form_answers": dict(dispute.intake),
 118→    }
 119→
 120→
 121→def run_dispute(
 122→    *,
 123→    dispute: Dispute,
 124→    llm: LLMClient,
 125→    policy: PolicySet,
 126→    events: EventLog,
 127→    confidence_threshold: float,
 128→    autonomous_cap_sgd: float = 50.00,
 129→) -> CaseFile:
 130→    """Run one dispute end to end and return its case file."""
 131→    events.emit(
 132→        EventType.RUN_STARTED,
 133→        from_=Actor.SYSTEM,
 134→        to=Actor.SYSTEM,
 135→        summary="run started for dispute %s (%s) with %s, threshold %.2f"
 136→        % (dispute.dispute_id, dispute.category, llm.provider_name, confidence_threshold),
 137→        payload={
 138→            "dispute_id": dispute.dispute_id,
 139→            "category": dispute.category,
 140→            "llm_provider": llm.provider_name,
 141→            "confidence_threshold": confidence_threshold,
 142→            "policy_path": _policy_source_path(policy),
 143→            "policy_rule_ids": policy.rule_ids(),
 144→        },
 145→    )
 146→
 147→    events.emit(
 148→        EventType.DISPUTE_FILED,
 149→        from_=dispute.filed_by,
 150→        to=Actor.SYSTEM,
 151→        summary="%s filed dispute %s as '%s'" % (dispute.filed_by, dispute.dispute_id, dispute.category_as_submitted),
 152→        payload=dispute.raw,
 153→    )
 154→
 155→    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- routing
 156→    if not dispute.is_agent_handled:
 157→        return _human_review(dispute=dispute, events=events, policy=policy, threshold=confidence_threshold)
 158→
 159→    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- evidence
 160→    pack = build_evidence_pack(dispute)
 161→    pack_event = events.emit(
 162→        EventType.EVIDENCE_PACK_BUILT,
 163→        from_=Actor.SYSTEM,
 164→        to="agents",
 165→        summary="Evidence Pack built: %d computed field(s) available to cite" % len(pack.field_refs()),
 166→        payload=pack.to_dict(),
 167→    )
 168→
 169→    rider = RiderAdvocate(llm=llm, events=events, policy=policy)
 170→    driver = DriverAdvocate(llm=llm, events=events, policy=policy)
 171→    judge = Judge(llm=llm, events=events, policy=policy)
 172→
 173→    for advocate in (rider, driver):
 174→        events.emit(
 175→            EventType.CASE_ASSIGNED,
 176→            from_=Actor.SYSTEM,
 177→            to=advocate.name,
 178→            summary="case assigned to the %s" % advocate.role_title,
 179→            payload={
 180→                "dispute_id": dispute.dispute_id,
 181→                "category": dispute.category,
 182→                "evidence_pack_ref": pack_event.payload_ref,
 183→            },
 184→        )
 185→
 186→    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- advocates
 187→    rider_case = rider.run(dispute, pack)
 188→    driver_case = driver.run(dispute, pack)
 189→
 190→    events.emit(
 191→        EventType.JUDGE_DELIBERATION_STARTED,
 192→        from_=Actor.SYSTEM,
 193→        to=judge.name,
 194→        summary="both cases with the Judge for deliberation",
 195→        payload={
 196→            "dispute_id": dispute.dispute_id,
 197→            "rider_case_agent": rider_case.agent,
 198→            "driver_case_agent": driver_case.agent,
 199→            "rider_requested": _requested(rider_case),
 200→            "driver_requested": _requested(driver_case),
 201→        },
 202→    )
 203→
 204→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- judge
 205→    resolution = judge.run(
 206→        dispute,
 207→        pack,
 208→        rider_case,
 209→        driver_case,
 210→        confidence_threshold=confidence_threshold,
 211→        autonomous_cap_sgd=autonomous_cap_sgd,
 212→    )
 213→
 214→    events.emit(
 215→        EventType.PARTY_NOTIFIED,
 216→        from_=Actor.SYSTEM,
 217→        to=Actor.PARTIES,
 218→        summary="parties notified: %s" % _outcome_phrase(resolution),
 219→        payload={
 220→            "dispute_id": dispute.dispute_id,
 221→            "outcome": resolution.outcome,
 222→            "message": resolution.party_message,
 223→        },
 224→    )
 225→
 226→    case_file = CaseFile(
 227→        run_id=events.run_id,
 228→        dispute_id=dispute.dispute_id,
 229→        category=dispute.category,
 230→        generated_at=_now(),
 231→        confidence_threshold=confidence_threshold,
 232→        policy_path=_policy_source_path(policy),
 233→        policy_rule_ids=policy.rule_ids(),
 234→        intake=_intake_section(dispute),
 235→        evidence_pack=pack.to_dict(),
 236→        rider_case=rider_case.to_dict(),
 237→        driver_case=driver_case.to_dict(),
 238→        resolution=resolution.to_dict(),
 239→    )
 240→    _complete(events, case_file, resolution)
 241→    return case_file
 242→
 243→
 244→# ------------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
 245→
 246→
 247→def _now() -> str:
 248→    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")
 249→
 250→
 251→def _requested(case: AdvocateCase) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 252→    return {"outcome": case.requested_outcome, "amount_sgd": case.requested_amount_sgd}
 253→
 254→
 255→def _outcome_phrase(resolution: Resolution) -> str:
 256→    if resolution.ruling is not None:
 257→        return "%s of SGD %.2f" % (resolution.ruling.action, resolution.ruling.recommended_amount_sgd)
 258→    return "your case is still under review"
 259→
 260→
 261→def _human_review(
 262→    *, dispute: Dispute, events: EventLog, policy: PolicySet, threshold: float
 263→) -> CaseFile:
 264→    """A category outside the two locked ones: human queue, neutral message, no agents."""
 265→    events.emit(
 266→        EventType.DISPUTE_ROUTED_TO_HUMAN_REVIEW,
 267→        from_=Actor.SYSTEM,
 268→        to=Actor.HUMAN_REVIEW,
 269→        summary="category '%s' is outside the two handled categories; queued for human review"
 270→        % dispute.category_as_submitted,
 271→        payload={
 272→            "dispute_id": dispute.dispute_id,
 273→            "category_as_submitted": dispute.category_as_submitted,
 274→            "reason": "no agent is scoped to handle this category",
 275→        },
 276→    )
 277→    resolution = Resolution(
 278→        dispute_id=dispute.dispute_id,
 279→        outcome=OUTCOME_HUMAN_REVIEW,
 280→        party_message=HUMAN_REVIEW_MESSAGE,
 281→        confidence_threshold=threshold,
 282→        escalated_for_human_review=True,
 283→        notes=["routed to human review: category outside the two the agents handle"],
 284→    )
 285→    events.emit(
 286→        EventType.PARTY_NOTIFIED,
 287→        from_=Actor.SYSTEM,
 288→        to=Actor.PARTIES,
 289→        summary="parties notified: passed to the support team",
 290→        payload={
 291→            "dispute_id": dispute.dispute_id,
 292→            "outcome": resolution.outcome,
 293→            "message": resolution.party_message,
 294→        },
 295→    )
 296→
 297→    case_file = CaseFile(
 298→        run_id=events.run_id,
 299→        dispute_id=dispute.dispute_id,
 300→        category=dispute.category,
 301→        generated_at=_now(),
 302→        confidence_threshold=threshold,
 303→        policy_path=_policy_source_path(policy),
 304→        policy_rule_ids=policy.rule_ids(),
 305→        intake=_intake_section(dispute),
 306→        evidence_pack=None,
 307→        rider_case=None,
 308→        driver_case=None,
 309→        resolution=resolution.to_dict(),
 310→    )
 311→    _complete(events, case_file, resolution)
 312→    return case_file
 313→
 314→
 315→def _complete(events: EventLog, case_file: CaseFile, resolution: Resolution) -> None:
 316→    case_file.events = events.snapshot()
 317→    events.emit(
 318→        EventType.RUN_COMPLETED,
 319→        from_=Actor.SYSTEM,
 320→        to=Actor.SYSTEM,
 321→        summary="run completed: %s" % resolution.outcome,
 322→        payload={
 323→            "dispute_id": case_file.dispute_id,
 324→            "outcome": resolution.outcome,
 325→            "delivered_to_parties": resolution.delivered_to_parties,
 326→            "escalated_for_human_review": resolution.escalated_for_human_review,
 327→        },
 328→    )
 329→    case_file.events = events.snapshot()

1→"""The dispute record: what the intake form submits, and how it is routed.
   2→
   3→Two record shapes are accepted, and the shape is detected from the record itself — an
   4→organiser record carries a top-level "dispute_ticket" object, ours does not. Everything
   5→downstream of this module sees one shape: the Dispute fields below.
   6→
   7→Shape 1 — Ryde's own (the intake form's output, and data/packs/ryde-synth-v1/):
   8→
   9→{
  10→  "dispute_id": "RD-0001",                    required, string
  11→  "category": "route_deviation",              required; see routing below
  12→  "filed_by": "rider",                        required; "rider" | "driver" (case/space tolerant)
  13→  "filed_at": "2026-09-20T09:15:00+08:00",
  14→  "claim":  {"text": "...", "amount_sgd": 6.40},
  15→  "intake": {"<form question>": "<answer>"},  raw intake-form answers, pass-through
  16→  "trip": {
  17→     "trip_id": "T-1", "rider_id": "r-1", "driver_id": "d-1",
  18→     "requested_at"/"pickup_at"/"dropoff_at": ISO-8601,
  19→     "estimated_duration_min": 18, "estimated_distance_km": 7.2,
  20→     "actual_distance_km": 9.4,               optional; else derived from actual_route
  21→     "actual_route": [{"lat": 1.3, "lng": 103.8, "t": "..."}, ...],
  22→     "fare": {
  23→        "charged_sgd": 14.80,
  24→        "breakdown": {"base_sgd": 3.20, "distance_sgd": 7.10, "time_sgd": 2.30,
  25→                      "surge_sgd": 1.20, "promo_sgd": 1.00, "platform_fee_sgd": 0.80},
  26→        "rates": {"base_sgd": 3.20, "per_km_sgd": 0.80, "per_min_sgd": 0.25,
  27→                  "surge_multiplier": 1.2}
  28→     }
  29→  },
  30→  "cancellation": {
  31→     "driver_arrived_at": "...", "wait_started_at": "...", "cancelled_at": "...",
  32→     "driver_wait_minutes": 5.5, "cancellation_fee_sgd": 4.00,
  33→     "driver_marked_no_show": true, "rider_claims_driver_absent": true,
  34→     "driver_gps_at_arrival": {"lat": .., "lng": ..}, "pickup_point": {"lat": .., "lng": ..}
  35→  },
  36→  "chat_log": [{"t": "...", "sender": "rider", "text": "..."}, ...],
  37→  "profiles": {"rider": {...}, "driver": {...}}
  38→}
  39→
  40→Everything except dispute_id, category and filed_by is optional; missing blocks produce an
  41→Evidence Pack with null fields and an explanatory note, rather than a guess.
  42→
  43→Shape 2 — the organisers' (data/packs/organiser-style-v1/, and their own DISP-002):
  44→
  45→{
  46→  "dispute_ticket": {
  47→     "dispute_id": "DISP-002", "trip_id": "TRIP-...", "filed_by": "rider",
  48→     "dispute_type": "no_show_charge",        -> category (via normalise_category)
  49→     "description": "...",                    -> claim.text when ryde_extensions has none
  50→     "filed_at": "...", "status": "open"
  51→  },
  52→  "rider_profile" / "driver_profile": {...},  -> profiles.rider / profiles.driver
  53→  "trip_data": {...},                         -> trip
  54→  "gps_telemetry": [{"timestamp", "lat", "lng", "speed_kmh", "status"}, ...],
  55→  "chat_logs": [{"timestamp", "sender", "type", "content"}, ...],   -> chat_log
  56→  "app_events": [{"timestamp", "event_type", "details"}, ...],
  57→  "cancellation_policy": {...},               -> cancellation.case_policy, untouched
  58→  "ryde_extensions": {...}                    our fields their shape has no slot for
  59→}
  60→
  61→`_organiser_to_record` is the whole of that mapping, in one function, so a wrong line
  62→shows up as a mismatched Evidence Pack field rather than as a wrong ruling later. Two
  63→substitutions are deliberately never made, because each one would silently change rulings:
  64→
  65→  * matched_at comes from the app_events entry with event_type "driver_assigned", or is
  66→    left out. Booking time is not matching time; the Evidence Pack already flags a
  67→    booking-time anchor as a proxy, and inventing one here would hide that (the NS-1
  68→    defect of 2026-09-21).
  69→  * driver_gps_at_arrival comes from the gps_telemetry row whose status is "arrived", or
  70→    is left out. A missing arrival position is what escalates NS-0205; a position
  71→    borrowed from the pickup point or the last row would rule the case instead.
  72→  * rider_claims_driver_absent comes from ryde_extensions, or is left out. Whether the
  73→    rider says the driver never came is never inferred from who filed the dispute: the
  74→    rider's own words stay in claim.text for the Advocates, and the structured field
  75→    says "not stated" unless the record states it (the session-five review).
  76→
  77→Routing: only the two locked categories reach the agents. Anything else — including the
  78→form's "other" option, the statement's out-of-scope categories, and any value the corpus
  79→does not use — goes to the human-review queue with a neutral message.
  80→"""
  81→
  82→from __future__ import annotations
  83→
  84→import json
  85→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  86→from pathlib import Path
  87→from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
  88→
  89→CATEGORY_ROUTE_DEVIATION = "route_deviation"
  90→CATEGORY_NO_SHOW_CHARGE = "no_show_charge"
  91→CATEGORY_OTHER = "other"
  92→
  93→#: Categories the three agents handle end to end. Nothing else, by locked scope.
  94→AGENT_CATEGORIES = (CATEGORY_ROUTE_DEVIATION, CATEGORY_NO_SHOW_CHARGE)
  95→
  96→_ALIASES = {
  97→    "route_deviation": CATEGORY_ROUTE_DEVIATION,
  98→    "route_deviation_claim": CATEGORY_ROUTE_DEVIATION,
  99→    "deviation": CATEGORY_ROUTE_DEVIATION,
 100→    "longer_route": CATEGORY_ROUTE_DEVIATION,
 101→    "no_show_charge": CATEGORY_NO_SHOW_CHARGE,
 102→    "no_show": CATEGORY_NO_SHOW_CHARGE,
 103→    "noshow": CATEGORY_NO_SHOW_CHARGE,
 104→    "no_show_fee": CATEGORY_NO_SHOW_CHARGE,
 105→    "cancellation_fee": CATEGORY_NO_SHOW_CHARGE,
 106→    "other": CATEGORY_OTHER,
 107→    "property_damage": CATEGORY_OTHER,
 108→    "property_damage_mess": CATEGORY_OTHER,
 109→    "safety_incident": CATEGORY_OTHER,
 110→}
 111→
 112→
 113→class DisputeError(ValueError):
 114→    """The submitted dispute record is not usable."""
 115→
 116→
 117→def normalise_category(value: Any) -> str:
 118→    """Map a submitted category onto one of the three routing buckets.
 119→
 120→    Unknown values route to `other` (human review) rather than raising: the system must
 121→    never let an unrecognised category reach an agent that was not scoped to handle it.
 122→    """
 123→    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
 124→        raise DisputeError("dispute category is required and must be a non-empty string")
 125→    key = value.strip().lower().replace("-", "_").replace(" ", "_")
 126→    return _ALIASES.get(key, CATEGORY_OTHER)
 127→
 128→
 129→@dataclass(frozen=True)
 130→class Dispute:
 131→    """One filed dispute, parsed and routed."""
 132→
 133→    dispute_id: str
 134→    category: str
 135→    category_as_submitted: str
 136→    filed_by: str
 137→    filed_at: Optional[str]
 138→    claim: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
 139→    intake: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
 140→    trip: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
 141→    cancellation: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

 188→def _copy_present(target: Dict[str, Any], source: Dict[str, Any], key: str, as_key: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
 189→    """Carry a field across under its own name or a renamed one, when it is there.
 190→
 191→    A missing key stays missing rather than becoming an explicit null: the Evidence Pack
 192→    distinguishes "the record does not state this" from "the record states null", and only
 193→    the first is true here.

 200→def _event_timestamp(events: Any, event_type: str) -> Optional[str]:
 201→    """The timestamp of the app_events entry of this type, or None if there is no such entry."""
 202→    for event in events if isinstance(events, list) else []:
 203→        if isinstance(event, dict) and event.get("event_type") == event_type:
 204→            timestamp = event.get("timestamp")

 210→def _arrival_position(telemetry: Any) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
 211→    """The {lat, lng} of the telemetry row whose status is "arrived", or None.
 212→
 213→    None is a real answer — NS-0205's record has no arrival row, and that absence is the
 214→    evidence that escalates the case. Substituting the pickup point or the last row would
 215→    supply a position the record does not contain.
 216→    """
 217→    for row in telemetry if isinstance(telemetry, list) else []:
 218→        if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get("status") == "arrived":
 219→            lat, lng = row.get("lat"), row.get("lng")
 220→            if isinstance(lat, (int, float)) and isinstance(lng, (int, float)):
 221→                return {"lat": lat, "lng": lng}

 225→def _organiser_profile(party: str, raw: Any) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
 226→    """One side's profile, in our field names. None when the record has no such block."""
 227→    profile = _object(raw)
 228→    if not profile:
 229→        return None
 230→    history = _object(profile.get("dispute_history"))
 231→    mapped: Dict[str, Any] = {}
 232→    _copy_present(mapped, profile, "%s_id" % party, "party_id")
 233→    _copy_present(mapped, profile, "account_age_days")
 234→    _copy_present(mapped, profile, "total_trips", "trips_completed")
 235→    _copy_present(mapped, profile, "avg_rating", "rating")
 236→    _copy_present(mapped, profile, "fraud_flags")
 237→    _copy_present(mapped, history, "total_disputes", "disputes_total")
 238→    # A rider's history counts disputes they won ("upheld"); a driver's counts disputes
 239→    # lost against them ("upheld_against"). Both land on disputes_upheld, which is the
 240→    # field the pack turns into the upheld rate the agents argue from.
 241→    _copy_present(mapped, history, "upheld_against" if party == "driver" else "upheld", "disputes_upheld")

 245→def _organiser_to_record(data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 246→    """Translate one organisers'-shape record into our shape. See the module docstring."""
 247→    ticket = _object(data.get("dispute_ticket"))
 248→    trip_data = _object(data.get("trip_data"))
 249→    extensions = _object(data.get("ryde_extensions"))
 250→    category = normalise_category(ticket.get("dispute_type"))
 251→
 252→    # The claim and the intake answers live in our extension block; their own shape has no
 253→    # slot for either. Without the block (DISP-002) the description is all the party said,
 254→    # and no amount was asked for.
 255→    claim = extensions.get("claim")
 256→    if claim is None:
 257→        claim = {"text": ticket.get("description")}
 258→
 259→    trip: Dict[str, Any] = {}
 260→    for source, target in (
 261→        ("trip_id", "trip_id"),
 262→        ("rider_id", "rider_id"),
 263→        ("driver_id", "driver_id"),
 264→        ("estimated_duration_min", "estimated_duration_min"),
 265→        ("estimated_distance_km", "estimated_distance_km"),
 266→        ("requested_time", "requested_at"),
 267→        ("pickup_time", "pickup_at"),
 268→        ("dropoff_time", "dropoff_at"),
 269→    ):
 270→        _copy_present(trip, trip_data, source, target)
 271→    _copy_present(trip, extensions, "service_type")
 272→
 273→    if isinstance(trip_data.get("fare"), dict):
 274→        trip["fare"] = trip_data["fare"]
 275→    else:
 276→        # Their shape states a cancellation or waiting fee once, on trip_data; ours states
 277→        # it twice — on the cancellation block and as the charged amount in the fare
 278→        # breakdown. The reader places it in both, or the fee would vanish from the pack.
 279→        fee = trip_data.get("cancellation_fee")
 280→        if fee is None:
 281→            fee = trip_data.get("waiting_fee")
 282→        if fee is not None:
 283→            trip["fare"] = {"charged_sgd": fee, "breakdown": {"cancellation_sgd": fee}}
 284→
 285→    # Their gps_telemetry is the trip trace for a route case, but for a no-show it is the
 286→    # approach-and-wait trace: a route built from it would report a distance the trip never
 287→    # covered, so it becomes actual_route only where the trip actually ran.
 288→    if category == CATEGORY_ROUTE_DEVIATION:
 289→        route = [
 290→            {"lat": row.get("lat"), "lng": row.get("lng"), "t": row.get("timestamp")}
 291→            for row in (data.get("gps_telemetry") if isinstance(data.get("gps_telemetry"), list) else [])
 292→            if isinstance(row, dict)
 293→        ]
 294→        if route:
 295→            trip["actual_route"] = route
 296→
 297→    cancellation: Dict[str, Any] = {}
 298→    arrived_at = trip_data.get("driver_arrival_time")
 299→    wait_started_at = trip_data.get("driver_wait_start")
 300→    # A waiting fee is charged when the trip went ahead, so the boarding time is the
 301→    # moment the charge was incurred (NS-0207); otherwise it is the cancellation.
 302→    cancelled_at = trip_data.get("cancellation_time")
 303→    if cancelled_at is None:
 304→        cancelled_at = trip_data.get("rider_boarded_time")
 305→    fee = trip_data.get("cancellation_fee")
 306→    if fee is None:
 307→        fee = trip_data.get("waiting_fee")
 308→
 309→    has_cancellation_facts = any(
 310→        value is not None
 311→        for value in (
 312→            arrived_at,
 313→            wait_started_at,
 314→            cancelled_at,
 315→            fee,
 316→            trip_data.get("cancellation_reason"),
 317→        )
 318→    )
 319→    if has_cancellation_facts:
 320→        _copy_present(cancellation, trip_data, "driver_arrival_time", "driver_arrived_at")
 321→        _copy_present(cancellation, trip_data, "driver_wait_start", "wait_started_at")
 322→        if cancelled_at is not None:
 323→            cancellation["cancelled_at"] = cancelled_at
 324→        # Each fee is carried under its own name, so a record stating both loses
 325→        # neither (schema 1.3). cancellation_fee_sgd alone keeps the twin property:
 326→        # with no cancellation fee stated, the fee this reader places in the fare
 327→        # breakdown below (the waiting fee) stands in for comparison downstream.
 328→        if trip_data.get("cancellation_fee") is not None:
 329→            cancellation["cancellation_fee_sgd"] = trip_data["cancellation_fee"]
 330→        if trip_data.get("waiting_fee") is not None:
 331→            cancellation["waiting_fee_sgd"] = trip_data["waiting_fee"]
 332→        # Never the booking time: the pack's matching anchor names its source, and a proxy
 333→        # anchor invented here would be indistinguishable from a real one.
 334→        matched_at = _event_timestamp(data.get("app_events"), "driver_assigned")
 335→        if matched_at is not None:
 336→            cancellation["matched_at"] = matched_at
 337→        cancellation["driver_marked_no_show"] = trip_data.get("cancellation_reason") == "rider_no_show"
 338→        if "rider_claims_driver_absent" in extensions:
 339→            cancellation["rider_claims_driver_absent"] = extensions["rider_claims_driver_absent"]
 340→        # Never inferred: whether the rider says the driver never came is a structured
 341→        # fact only when the record states one (in ryde_extensions). Without it the field
 342→        # stays unset and the pack reports None — the rider's own words remain in
 343→        # claim.text, where the Advocates read them.
 344→        pickup = _object(trip_data.get("pickup_location"))
 345→        if "lat" in pickup and "lng" in pickup:
 346→            cancellation["pickup_point"] = {"lat": pickup.get("lat"), "lng": pickup.get("lng")}
 347→        position = _arrival_position(data.get("gps_telemetry"))
 348→        if position is not None:
 349→            cancellation["driver_gps_at_arrival"] = position
 350→        # The terms that govern this case, so the agents can see which policy the charge
 351→        # was applied under. Their shape carries it per case; passed through untouched.
 352→        if isinstance(data.get("cancellation_policy"), dict):
 353→            cancellation["case_policy"] = data["cancellation_policy"]
 354→
 355→    chat_log: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
 356→    for message in data.get("chat_logs") if isinstance(data.get("chat_logs"), list) else []:
 357→        if not isinstance(message, dict):
 358→            continue
 359→        entry: Dict[str, Any] = {
 360→            "t": message.get("timestamp"),
 361→            "sender": message.get("sender"),
 362→            "text": message.get("content"),
 363→        }
 364→        # A call is stronger evidence of a contact attempt than a message, and "type" is
 365→        # the only thing that tells them apart.
 366→        if "type" in message:
 367→            entry["type"] = message["type"]
 368→        chat_log.append(entry)
 369→
 370→    profiles: Dict[str, Any] = {}
 371→    for party in ("rider", "driver"):
 372→        profile = _organiser_profile(party, data.get("%s_profile" % party))
 373→        if profile is not None:
 374→            profiles[party] = profile
 375→
 376→    return {
 377→        "dispute_id": ticket.get("dispute_id"),
 378→        "category": ticket.get("dispute_type"),
 379→        "filed_by": ticket.get("filed_by"),
 380→        "filed_at": ticket.get("filed_at"),
 381→        "claim": claim,
 382→        "intake": extensions.get("intake") or {},
 383→        "trip": trip,
 384→        "cancellation": cancellation,
 385→        "chat_log": chat_log,
 386→        "profiles": profiles,
 387→    }

 393→def parse_dispute(data: Any) -> Dispute:
 394→    """Validate a raw dispute dict into a Dispute. Raises DisputeError with the reason."""
 395→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
 396→        raise DisputeError("a dispute record must be a JSON object")
 397→    # `raw` keeps the record exactly as it arrived, whichever shape that was: the case
 398→    # file's grievance section and the filed-dispute event show what was actually filed.
 399→    return _parse_record(_organiser_to_record(data) if is_organiser_record(data) else data, raw=data)
 400→
 401→
 402→def _parse_record(data: Dict[str, Any], raw: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dispute:
 403→    dispute_id = data.get("dispute_id")
 404→    if not isinstance(dispute_id, str) or not dispute_id.strip():
 405→        raise DisputeError("dispute_id is required and must be a non-empty string")
 406→
 407→    submitted_category = data.get("category")
 408→    category = normalise_category(submitted_category)
 409→
 410→    raw_filed_by = data.get("filed_by")
 411→    if not isinstance(raw_filed_by, str) or not raw_filed_by.strip():
 412→        raise DisputeError(
 413→            "filed_by is required and must be 'rider' or 'driver', not %r" % (raw_filed_by,)
 414→        )
 415→    filed_by = raw_filed_by.strip().lower()
 416→    if filed_by not in ("rider", "driver"):
 417→        raise DisputeError("filed_by must be 'rider' or 'driver', not %r" % raw_filed_by)
 418→
 419→    chat_log = data.get("chat_log") or []
 420→    if not isinstance(chat_log, list):
 421→        raise DisputeError("dispute field 'chat_log' must be a list")
 422→
 423→    filed_at = data.get("filed_at")
 424→    return Dispute(
 425→        dispute_id=dispute_id.strip(),
 426→        category=category,
 427→        category_as_submitted=str(submitted_category),
 428→        filed_by=filed_by,
 429→        filed_at=filed_at if isinstance(filed_at, str) else None,
 430→        claim=_mapping(data.get("claim"), "claim"),
 431→        intake=_mapping(data.get("intake"), "intake"),
 432→        trip=_mapping(data.get("trip"), "trip"),
 433→        cancellation=_mapping(data.get("cancellation"), "cancellation"),
 434→        chat_log=[item for item in chat_log if isinstance(item, dict)],
 435→        profiles=_mapping(data.get("profiles"), "profiles"),
 436→        raw=dict(raw),
 437→    )

 440→def load_dispute(path: Path) -> Dispute:
 441→    """Read and validate one dispute JSON file."""
 442→    dispute_path = Path(path)
 443→    if not dispute_path.exists():
 444→        raise DisputeError("dispute file not found: %s" % dispute_path)
 445→    try:
 446→        data = json.loads(dispute_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
 447→    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
 448→        raise DisputeError("dispute file is not valid JSON (%s): %s" % (dispute_path, exc)) from exc
 449→    return parse_dispute(data)

1→"""Shared agent scaffolding: prompts, the LLM call, and citation validation.
   2→
   3→Every agent gets the same material (the dispute intake, the Evidence Pack, the policy
   4→document) and the same hard rules, and every agent returns one JSON object matching its
   5→contract. The differences between agents are their role text and their output schema.
   6→
   7→The hard rules are the ones the locked scope demands: no arithmetic by an agent (every
   8→number comes from the pack), evidence cited by dotted field reference, policy cited by
   9→rule ID, and nothing invented. Citations are validated against the pack and the policy
  10→document after every call; anything that does not resolve is recorded on the case rather
  11→than quietly dropped, so the case file shows what the model actually claimed.
  12→"""
  13→
  14→from __future__ import annotations
  15→
  16→import abc
  17→import json
  18→from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
  19→
  20→from ..dispute import Dispute
  21→from ..events import EventLog
  22→from ..evidence import EvidencePack
  23→from ..llm import LLMClient, LLMContractError, LLMError, LLMRequest, parse_json_object
  24→from ..policy import PolicySet
  25→from ..schemas import AdvocateCase, ContractError
  26→
  27→#: Kept deliberately blunt: these are the rules a model is most likely to drift from.
  28→HARD_RULES = """HARD RULES
  29→1. Never do arithmetic. Every number you state must be copied verbatim from the Evidence
  30→   Pack. If a number you want is not in the pack, say it is unavailable — do not compute it.
  31→2. Cite evidence only by the exact dotted references listed under CITABLE EVIDENCE REFS.
  32→3. Cite policy only by rule IDs listed under POLICY RULE IDS. Never invent a rule ID.
  33→4. Return exactly one JSON object matching the schema below. No prose around it, no code
  34→   fence, no commentary."""
  35→
  36→
  37→class AgentError(RuntimeError):
  38→    """An agent could not complete its task."""
  39→
  40→
  41→def _json_block(value: Any) -> str:
  42→    return json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=False, default=str)
  43→
  44→
  45→def dispute_block(dispute: Dispute) -> str:
  46→    """The intake-form submission, as the parties filed it."""
  47→    lines = [
  48→        "dispute_id: %s" % dispute.dispute_id,
  49→        "category: %s" % dispute.category,
  50→        "filed_by: %s" % dispute.filed_by,
  51→        "filed_at: %s" % (dispute.filed_at or "not recorded"),
  52→        'claim: "%s"' % dispute.claim_text,
  53→        "amount_claimed_sgd: %s" % dispute.claim_amount_sgd,
  54→    ]
  55→    if dispute.intake:
  56→        lines.append("intake_form_answers:")
  57→        lines.append(_json_block(dispute.intake))
  58→    return "\n".join(lines)
  59→
  60→
  61→def evidence_block(pack: EvidencePack) -> str:
  62→    return _json_block(pack.to_dict())
  63→
  64→
  65→def citable_refs_block(pack: EvidencePack) -> str:
  66→    refs = pack.field_refs()
  67→    if not refs:
  68→        return "(none — the pack has no computed fields for this dispute)"
  69→    return "\n".join("- %s" % ref for ref in refs)
  70→
  71→
  72→def policy_blocks(policy: PolicySet) -> str:
  73→    return "POLICY DOCUMENT\n%s\n\nPOLICY RULE IDS\n%s" % (
  74→        policy.text.strip(),
  75→        ", ".join(policy.rule_ids()) or "(none)",
  76→    )
  77→
  78→
  79→def validate_citations(
  80→    *,
  81→    cited_refs: List[str],
  82→    cited_rules: List[str],
  83→    pack: EvidencePack,
  84→    policy: PolicySet,
  85→) -> Dict[str, Any]:
  86→    """Check every citation against the pack and the policy document.
  87→
  88→    Nothing is removed: the case keeps the model's own claims, and the failures are
  89→    recorded alongside them so the case file shows what was claimed and what resolved.
  90→    """
  91→    legal_refs = set(pack.field_refs())
  92→    unknown_refs = [ref for ref in cited_refs if ref not in legal_refs]
  93→    unknown_rules = policy.unknown_rule_ids(cited_rules)
  94→
  95→    notes: List[str] = []
  96→    if unknown_refs:
  97→        notes.append(
  98→            "%d cited evidence reference(s) do not resolve to a field in the pack" % len(unknown_refs)
  99→        )
 100→    if unknown_rules:
 101→        notes.append(
 102→            "%d cited policy rule ID(s) are not in the policy document" % len(unknown_rules)
 103→        )
 104→
 105→    return {
 106→        "unknown_evidence_refs": unknown_refs,
 107→        "unknown_rule_ids": unknown_rules,
 108→        "notes": notes,

 112→class BaseAgent(abc.ABC):
 113→    """Common behaviour: build the prompt, make the call, parse, validate."""
 114→
 115→    name = "agent"
 116→    role_title = "Agent"
 117→
 118→    def __init__(self, llm: LLMClient, events: EventLog, policy: PolicySet):
 119→        self.llm = llm
 120→        self.events = events
 121→        self.policy = policy
 122→
 123→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ to override
 124→
 125→    @abc.abstractmethod
 126→    def system_prompt(self) -> str:
 127→        """Role, hard rules and output schema for this agent."""
 128→
 129→    # -------------------------------------------------------------------- LLM call
 130→
 131→    def _ask(
 132→        self,
 133→        *,
 134→        system_prompt: str,
 135→        user_prompt: str,
 136→        metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
 137→    ) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], Dict[str, Any]]:
 138→        """One LLM call, parsed into a JSON object. Returns (payload, provenance)."""
 139→        request = LLMRequest(
 140→            agent=self.name,
 141→            system_prompt=system_prompt,
 142→            user_prompt=user_prompt,
 143→            metadata=dict(metadata or {}),
 144→        )
 145→        try:
 146→            response = self.llm.complete(request)
 147→        except LLMError as exc:
 148→            raise AgentError("%s: the LLM call failed: %s" % (self.name, exc)) from exc
 149→
 150→        try:
 151→            payload = parse_json_object(response.text, agent=self.name)
 152→        except LLMContractError as exc:
 153→            raise AgentError("%s: the model response did not match the contract: %s" % (self.name, exc)) from exc
 154→
 155→        provenance = response.as_log_fields()
 156→        provenance["request_fingerprint"] = request.fingerprint()
 157→        return payload, provenance

 160→class AdvocateAgent(BaseAgent):

 163→    The two advocates are separate agents with separate calls — one argues for the rider,
 164→    one for the driver — and neither sees the other's case.

 166→

 210→
 211→    def run(self, dispute: Dispute, pack: EvidencePack) -> AdvocateCase:
 212→        """Build this side's case, record the traffic, return the typed case."""
 213→        payload, llm_info = self._ask(
 214→            system_prompt=self.system_prompt(),
 215→            user_prompt=self.user_prompt(dispute, pack),
 216→            metadata={
 217→                "party": self.party,
 218→                "dispute_id": dispute.dispute_id,
 219→                "category": dispute.category,
 220→                "claim_amount_sgd": dispute.claim_amount_sgd,
 221→                "available_evidence_refs": pack.field_refs(),
 222→                "available_rule_ids": self.policy.rule_ids(),
 223→            },
 224→        )
 225→
 226→        try:
 227→            case = AdvocateCase.from_payload(
 228→                payload,
 229→                party=self.party,
 230→                agent=self.name,
 231→                llm=llm_info,
 232→                validation=validate_citations(
 233→                    cited_refs=_string_list(payload.get("evidence_cited")),
 234→                    cited_rules=_string_list(payload.get("policy_rule_ids")),
 235→                    pack=pack,
 236→                    policy=self.policy,
 237→                ),
 238→            )
 239→        except ContractError as exc:
 240→            raise AgentError("%s returned a response that breaks its contract: %s" % (self.name, exc)) from exc
 241→
 242→        self.events.emit(
 243→            "advocate.case_submitted",
 244→            from_=self.name,
 245→            to="judge",
 246→            summary="%s submitted a case citing %d evidence field(s) and %d rule(s)"
 247→            % (self.role_title, len(case.evidence_cited), len(case.policy_rule_ids)),
 248→            payload=case.to_dict(),
 249→        )
 250→
 251→        if case.follow_up_questions:
 252→            self.events.emit(
 253→                "advocate.follow_up_requested",
 254→                from_=self.name,
 255→                to=dispute.filed_by,
 256→                summary="%s asked the %s %d follow-up question(s)"
 257→                % (self.role_title, dispute.filed_by, len(case.follow_up_questions)),
 258→                payload={
 259→                    "dispute_id": dispute.dispute_id,
 260→                    "party": dispute.filed_by,
 261→                    "questions": case.follow_up_questions,
 262→                    "reason": "data conflicting or insufficient on the submitted form",
 263→                },
 264→            )
 265→
 266→        return case
 267→
 268→
 269→def _string_list(value: Any) -> List[str]:
 270→    """Best-effort list of strings for pre-validation, without raising on odd shapes."""
 271→    if not isinstance(value, list):
 272→        return []
 273→    return [item.strip() for item in value if isinstance(item, str) and item.strip()]

1→"""Deterministic mock LLM — proves the pipeline plumbing with no API key.
   2→
   3→This is NOT a model. It is a mechanical stand-in that returns responses shaped exactly
   4→like the agent contracts, so the pipeline, the event stream and the tests can be
   5→exercised before a real Tencent endpoint is pinned. Every string it returns is prefixed
   6→"MOCK" so a mock run can never be mistaken for a real ruling.
   7→
   8→It is deterministic on purpose: same dispute in, byte-identical case file out, which is
   9→what makes the end-to-end test meaningful.
  10→"""
  11→
  12→from __future__ import annotations
  13→
  14→import json
  15→from typing import Any, Dict, List
  16→
  17→from .base import LLMClient, LLMError, LLMRequest, LLMResponse
  18→
  19→MOCK_MARKER = "MOCK"
  20→
  21→
  22→def _pick(items: Any, count: int) -> List[Any]:
  23→    if not isinstance(items, list):
  24→        return []
  25→    return items[:count]
  26→
  27→
  28→class MockLLMClient(LLMClient):
  29→    """Returns contract-shaped canned responses.
  30→
  31→    judge_confidence is configurable so tests can drive the pipeline through the
  32→    low-confidence gate (below threshold -> no ruling, neutral message to the parties).
  33→    """
  34→
  35→    provider_name = "mock"
  36→
  37→    def __init__(self, judge_confidence: float = 0.86, model: str = "mock-llm-v0", **_ignored: Any):
  38→        if not 0.0 <= float(judge_confidence) <= 1.0:
  39→            raise LLMError("mock judge_confidence must be between 0 and 1")
  40→        self.judge_confidence = float(judge_confidence)
  41→        self.model = model
  42→        self.calls: List[LLMRequest] = []
  43→
  44→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ interface
  45→
  46→    def complete(self, request: LLMRequest) -> LLMResponse:
  47→        self.calls.append(request)
  48→        builder = {
  49→            "rider_advocate": self._advocate_response,
  50→            "driver_advocate": self._advocate_response,
  51→            "judge": self._judge_response,
  52→        }.get(request.agent)
  53→        if builder is None:
  54→            raise LLMError("mock has no canned response for agent %r" % request.agent)
  55→
  56→        payload = builder(request)
  57→        return LLMResponse(
  58→            text=json.dumps(payload, indent=2),
  59→            provider=self.provider_name,
  60→            model=self.model,
  61→            usage={"prompt_tokens": 0, "completion_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0, "mocked": True},
  62→            finish_reason="mock",
  63→        )
  64→
  65→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- builders
  66→
  67→    def _advocate_response(self, request: LLMRequest) -> Dict[str, Any]:
  68→        meta = request.metadata
  69→        party = str(meta.get("party") or "rider")
  70→        dispute_id = str(meta.get("dispute_id") or "unknown")
  71→        category = str(meta.get("category") or "unknown")
  72→        refs = _pick(meta.get("available_evidence_refs"), 3)
  73→        rule_ids = _pick(meta.get("available_rule_ids"), 2)
  74→        claim_amount = float(meta.get("claim_amount_sgd") or 0.0)
  75→
  76→        if party == "rider":
  77→            requested_outcome = "refund"
  78→            requested_amount = claim_amount
  79→        else:
  80→            requested_outcome = "no action"
  81→            requested_amount = 0.0
  82→
  83→        cited = ", ".join(refs) if refs else "no evidence fields available"
  84→        return {
  85→            "claim_summary": (
  86→                "%s Advocate %s case for dispute %s (%s)."
  87→                % (MOCK_MARKER, party, dispute_id, category)
  88→            ),
  89→            "evidence_cited": refs,
  90→            "policy_rule_ids": rule_ids,
  91→            "argument": (
  92→                "%s deterministic stand-in for the %s Advocate. It cites the evidence "
  93→                "pack fields it was given (%s) and the policy rules it was given (%s). "
  94→                "No arithmetic is performed here: every number is read from the pack."
  95→                % (MOCK_MARKER, party, cited, ", ".join(rule_ids) or "none")
  96→            ),
  97→            "requested_outcome": requested_outcome,
  98→            "requested_amount_sgd": requested_amount,
  99→            "follow_up_questions": [],
 100→        }
 101→
 102→    def _judge_response(self, request: LLMRequest) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 103→        meta = request.metadata
 104→        rule_ids = _pick(meta.get("available_rule_ids"), 2)
 105→        refs = _pick(meta.get("available_evidence_refs"), 3)
 106→        claim_amount = float(meta.get("claim_amount_sgd") or 0.0)
 107→
 108→        if claim_amount > 0.0:
 109→            action = "refund"
 110→            amount = claim_amount
 111→        else:
 112→            action = "no action"
 113→            amount = 0.0
 114→
 115→        return {
 116→            "action": action,
 117→            "recommended_amount_sgd": amount,
 118→            "confidence": self.judge_confidence,
 119→            "explanation": (
 120→                "%s deterministic stand-in for the Judge. It weighs the two advocate cases "
 121→                "it was given and applies the policy rules it was given (%s). The amount is "
 122→                "read from the evidence pack, not computed here."
 123→                % (MOCK_MARKER, ", ".join(rule_ids) or "none")
 124→            ),
 125→            "cited_rule_ids": rule_ids,
 126→            "cited_evidence_refs": refs,
 127→        }

1→"""Append-only event log — the observable inter-agent communication surface.
   2→
   3→The challenge statement requires inter-agent communication to be observable: a judge
   4→must be able to see how the agents exchange information and build their cases. This
   5→module is that record. It is built now, before any UI, because it is a hard requirement
   6→and because a run that was not recorded cannot be reconstructed afterwards.
   7→
   8→Storage layout for one run (default `<out_dir>/<run_id>/`):
   9→
  10→    events.jsonl                 one JSON object per line, append-only, never rewritten
  11→    payloads/<seq>-<type>.json   the full payload an event points at
  12→
  13→The event strip in the UI reads events.jsonl and shows one line per event; clicking an
  14→event opens its payload file. That is what `payload_ref` is for.
  15→
  16→Stable event schema (schema_version 1.0) — every event carries exactly these fields:
  17→
  18→    schema_version  str   "1.0"
  19→    seq             int   1-based, monotonic within the run
  20→    ts              str   UTC ISO-8601 with milliseconds and offset
  21→    run_id          str   identifies the run
  22→    type            str   dotted event type, from EventType below
  23→    from            str   actor the event came from
  24→    to              str   actor the event is addressed to
  25→    summary         str   one-line, human-readable — what the strip shows
  26→    payload_ref     str?  path to the payload file, relative to the run dir; null if none
  27→
  28→Adding a field is a schema_version change. Removing or renaming one is too.
  29→"""
  30→
  31→from __future__ import annotations
  32→
  33→import json
  34→import re
  35→from dataclasses import dataclass
  36→from datetime import datetime, timezone
  37→from pathlib import Path
  38→from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
  39→
  40→EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = "1.0"
  41→
  42→EVENTS_FILENAME = "events.jsonl"
  43→PAYLOADS_DIRNAME = "payloads"
  44→
  45→
  46→class EventType:
  47→    """Dotted event types. Constants, not free strings, so the strip stays filterable."""
  48→
  49→    RUN_STARTED = "run.started"
  50→    DISPUTE_FILED = "dispute.filed"
  51→    DISPUTE_ROUTED_TO_HUMAN_REVIEW = "dispute.routed_to_human_review"
  52→    EVIDENCE_PACK_BUILT = "evidence.pack_built"
  53→    CASE_ASSIGNED = "case.assigned"
  54→    ADVOCATE_CASE_SUBMITTED = "advocate.case_submitted"
  55→    ADVOCATE_FOLLOW_UP_REQUESTED = "advocate.follow_up_requested"
  56→    JUDGE_DELIBERATION_STARTED = "judge.deliberation_started"
  57→    JUDGE_RULING_ISSUED = "judge.ruling_issued"
  58→    JUDGE_RULING_WITHHELD = "judge.ruling_withheld"
  59→    PARTY_NOTIFIED = "party.notified"
  60→    RUN_COMPLETED = "run.completed"
  61→
  62→
  63→class Actor:
  64→    """Who events come from and go to. Parties are spectators and never act."""
  65→
  66→    SYSTEM = "system"
  67→    RIDER_ADVOCATE = "rider_advocate"
  68→    DRIVER_ADVOCATE = "driver_advocate"
  69→    JUDGE = "judge"
  70→    RIDER = "rider"
  71→    DRIVER = "driver"
  72→    PARTIES = "parties"
  73→    HUMAN_REVIEW = "human_review"
  74→
  75→
  76→@dataclass(frozen=True)
  77→class Event:
  78→    """One line of the log."""
  79→
  80→    schema_version: str
  81→    seq: int
  82→    ts: str
  83→    run_id: str
  84→    type: str
  85→    from_: str
  86→    to: str
  87→    summary: str
  88→    payload_ref: Optional[str] = None
  89→
  90→    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
  91→        """Wire form. The 'from' key is spelled out here because it is a Python keyword."""
  92→        return {
  93→            "schema_version": self.schema_version,
  94→            "seq": self.seq,
  95→            "ts": self.ts,
  96→            "run_id": self.run_id,
  97→            "type": self.type,
  98→            "from": self.from_,
  99→            "to": self.to,
 100→            "summary": self.summary,
 101→            "payload_ref": self.payload_ref,
 102→        }
 103→
 104→
 105→def _slug(value: str) -> str:
 106→    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", value.lower()).strip("-") or "event"
 107→
 108→
 109→class EventLog:
 110→    """Append-only writer for one run.
 111→
 112→    emit() is the only way in. Nothing here rewrites or deletes a line: the log is the
 113→    evidence, so a rerun writes a new run directory rather than editing an old one.
 114→    """
 115→
 116→    def __init__(self, run_dir: Path, run_id: str):
 117→        self.run_dir = Path(run_dir)
 118→        self.run_id = run_id
 119→        self.events_path = self.run_dir / EVENTS_FILENAME
 120→        self.payloads_dir = self.run_dir / PAYLOADS_DIRNAME
 121→        self._events: List[Event] = []
 122→
 123→        self.run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 124→        self.payloads_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 125→
 126→    # -------------------------------------------------------------------- writing
 127→
 128→    def emit(
 129→        self,
 130→        event_type: str,
 131→        *,
 132→        from_: str,
 133→        to: str,
 134→        summary: str,
 135→        payload: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
 136→    ) -> Event:
 137→        """Append one event, writing its payload file first so the ref is never dangling."""
 138→        seq = len(self._events) + 1
 139→        payload_ref = None
 140→        if payload is not None:
 141→            filename = "%04d-%s.json" % (seq, _slug(event_type))
 142→            payload_path = self.payloads_dir / filename
 143→            payload_path.write_text(
 144→                json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=False, default=str) + "\n",
 145→                encoding="utf-8",
 146→            )
 147→            payload_ref = "%s/%s" % (PAYLOADS_DIRNAME, filename)
 148→
 149→        event = Event(
 150→            schema_version=EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION,
 151→            seq=seq,
 152→            ts=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="milliseconds"),
 153→            run_id=self.run_id,
 154→            type=event_type,
 155→            from_=from_,
 156→            to=to,
 157→            summary=summary,
 158→            payload_ref=payload_ref,
 159→        )
 160→
 161→        with self.events_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
 162→            handle.write(json.dumps(event.to_dict(), default=str) + "\n")
 163→
 164→        self._events.append(event)
 165→        return event
 166→
 167→    # -------------------------------------------------------------------- reading
 168→
 169→    def events(self) -> List[Event]:
 170→        """Events emitted in this process, in order."""
 171→        return list(self._events)
 172→
 173→    def snapshot(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
 174→        """In-memory events as wire dicts — what the UI strip renders."""
 175→        return [event.to_dict() for event in self._events]
 176→
 177→    def read_payload(self, event: Event) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 178→        """Follow an event's payload_ref. Raises if the ref is missing or unreadable."""
 179→        if not event.payload_ref:
 180→            raise FileNotFoundError("event %d (%s) has no payload" % (event.seq, event.type))
 181→        return json.loads((self.run_dir / event.payload_ref).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
 182→
 183→    @staticmethod
 184→    def read_events(run_dir: Path) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
 185→        """Read events.jsonl back from disk — the UI's entry point, and the tests'."""
 186→        path = Path(run_dir) / EVENTS_FILENAME
 187→        if not path.exists():
 188→            raise FileNotFoundError("no event log at %s" % path)
 189→        events = []
 190→        for line_number, line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), start=1):
 191→            if not line.strip():
 192→                continue
 193→            try:
 194→                events.append(json.loads(line))
 195→            except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
 196→                raise ValueError("corrupt event log at line %d of %s" % (line_number, path)) from exc
 197→        return events

1→"""Command-line entry point.
   2→
   3→    python -m app.cli --dispute NS-0201                       # id in the default pack
   4→    python -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0101   # id in a named pack
   5→    python -m app.cli --dispute data/packs/ryde-synth-v1/disputes/RD-0101.json
   6→    python -m app.cli --dispute <path> --policy docs/policy.md --llm tencent
   7→
   8→--dispute takes either a path to a record file, as it always has, or a bare dispute id,
   9→which is looked up as <pack_dir>/disputes/<id>.json in the selected pack. The pack comes
  10→from app/config.json unless --pack names another one for this run.
  11→
  12→Runs one dispute through the full pipeline and writes the run's artifacts:
  13→
  14→    <out>/<run_id>/events.jsonl      append-only event log (the observable traffic)
  15→    <out>/<run_id>/payloads/*.json   full payload for each event
  16→    <out>/<run_id>/case_file.json    assembled record: evidence, claims, resolution, strip
  17→
  18→Defaults come from app/config.json; the flags override them for a single run.
  19→"""
  20→
  21→from __future__ import annotations
  22→
  23→import argparse
  24→import re
  25→import sys
  26→from datetime import datetime, timezone
  27→from pathlib import Path
  28→from typing import Optional, Sequence
  29→
  30→from .config import ConfigError, load_config, resolve_pack_dir
  31→from .dispute import DisputeError, load_dispute
  32→from .events import EventLog
  33→from .llm import LLMError, build_llm_client
  34→from .pipeline import run_dispute
  35→from .policy import PolicyError, load_policy
  36→
  37→EXIT_OK = 0
  38→EXIT_FAILED = 1
  39→
  40→
  41→def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
  42→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
  43→        prog="python -m app.cli",
  44→        description="Run one ride-hailing dispute through the multi-agent resolution pipeline.",
  45→    )
  46→    parser.add_argument(
  47→        "--dispute",
  48→        required=True,
  49→        help="a dispute id within the selected pack (e.g. NS-0201), or a path to a record file",
  50→    )
  51→    parser.add_argument(
  52→        "--pack",
  53→        default=None,
  54→        help="dataset pack to read disputes from, under data/packs/ (default: app/config.json)",
  55→    )
  56→    parser.add_argument(
  57→        "--policy", default=None, help="path to the policy document (default: app/config.json)"
  58→    )
  59→    parser.add_argument(
  60→        "--llm",
  61→        default=None,
  62→        choices=["mock", "tencent"],
  63→        help="LLM provider (default: app/config.json). 'mock' needs no API key.",
  64→    )
  65→    parser.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="output directory for run artifacts")
  66→    parser.add_argument("--run-id", default=None, help="override the generated run id")
  67→    return parser
  68→
  69→
  70→def _slug(value: str) -> str:
  71→    return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "-", value).strip("-") or "run"
  72→
  73→
  74→def dispute_path(value: str, pack_dir: Path) -> Path:
  75→    """Where --dispute points: a record file, or an id inside the selected pack.
  76→
  77→    Anything that names a file — an existing path, a path separator, or a .json suffix —
  78→    is used as given, so every command that worked before still means what it meant. A
  79→    bare token is a dispute id, which keeps the demo's commands short and makes the pack
  80→    the only place a case can come from.
  81→    """
  82→    if value.endswith(".json") or "/" in value or Path(value).exists():
  83→        return Path(value)
  84→    return Path(pack_dir) / "disputes" / ("%s.json" % value)
  85→
  86→
  87→def main(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> int:
  88→    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
  89→
  90→    try:
  91→        config = load_config()
  92→        pack_dir = resolve_pack_dir(args.pack) if args.pack else config.dataset_pack_dir
  93→        dispute = load_dispute(dispute_path(args.dispute, pack_dir))
  94→        policy = load_policy(Path(args.policy) if args.policy else config.policy_path)
  95→        provider = args.llm or config.llm.provider
  96→        llm = (
  97→            build_llm_client(provider, settings=config.llm)
  98→            if provider == "tencent"
  99→            else build_llm_client(provider)
 100→        )
 101→    except (ConfigError, DisputeError, PolicyError, LLMError) as exc:
 102→        print("error: %s" % exc, file=sys.stderr)
 103→        return EXIT_FAILED
 104→
 105→    out_dir = Path(args.out) if args.out else config.out_dir
 106→    run_id = args.run_id or "%s-%s" % (
 107→        datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ"),
 108→        _slug(dispute.dispute_id),
 109→    )
 110→    run_dir = out_dir / run_id
 111→    events = EventLog(run_dir, run_id)
 112→
 113→    try:
 114→        case_file = run_dispute(
 115→            dispute=dispute,
 116→            llm=llm,
 117→            policy=policy,
 118→            events=events,
 119→            confidence_threshold=config.confidence_threshold,
 120→            autonomous_cap_sgd=config.autonomous_cap_sgd,
 121→        )
 122→    except (DisputeError, PolicyError, LLMError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as exc:
 123→        print("error: the run failed: %s" % exc, file=sys.stderr)
 124→        print("partial event log: %s" % events.events_path, file=sys.stderr)
 125→        return EXIT_FAILED
 126→
 127→    case_path = case_file.write(run_dir)
 128→    _print_report(case_file, events, case_path)
 129→    return EXIT_OK
 130→

 132→def _print_report(case_file, events: EventLog, case_path: Path) -> None:
 133→    resolution = case_file.resolution
 134→    print("")
 135→    print("RYDE DISPUTE RESOLUTION — %s (%s)" % (case_file.dispute_id, case_file.category))
 136→    print("run: %s   llm: %s   threshold: %.2f"
 137→          % (case_file.run_id, resolution["ruling"]["llm"]["provider"] if resolution["ruling"] else "n/a",
 138→             case_file.confidence_threshold))
 139→    print("")
 140→    print("EVENT STRIP")
 141→    for event in events.snapshot():
 142→        print(
 143→            "%3d  %-24s %-18s -> %-16s %s"
 144→            % (event["seq"], event["ts"], event["from"], event["to"], event["summary"])
 145→        )
 146→    print("")
 147→    print("RESOLUTION")
 148→    print("  outcome:  %s" % resolution["outcome"])
 149→    if resolution["ruling"]:
 150→        ruling = resolution["ruling"]
 151→        print("  ruling:   %s of SGD %.2f (confidence %.2f)"
 152→              % (ruling["action"], ruling["recommended_amount_sgd"], ruling["confidence"]))
 153→        print("  rules:    %s" % (", ".join(ruling["cited_rule_ids"]) or "(none cited)"))
 154→    if resolution["withheld_candidate"]:
 155→        candidate = resolution["withheld_candidate"]
 156→        print("  withheld: %s of SGD %.2f at confidence %.2f — not delivered to the parties"
 157→              % (candidate["action"], candidate["recommended_amount_sgd"], candidate["confidence"]))
 158→    print("  parties:  %s" % resolution["party_message"])
 159→    print("")
 160→    print("ARTIFACTS")
 161→    print("  event log: %s" % events.events_path)
 162→    print("  case file: %s" % case_path)
 163→    print("")
 164→
 165→
 166→if __name__ == "__main__":
 167→    sys.exit(main())
